messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: GGIR version 1.2-5
parts:
I have now studied the issue I reported on the 9th of May in more
detail: It turns out that this was not a bug, but an intentionally
different definition of MVPA bouts. It has been two years since I
implemented that part of the code and I forgot why I implemented it in
the way I did, but there was actually some logic to it. Therefore, all
published estimates of time spent in MVPA bouts are as intended and in
line with the description in the respective articles.

The new way of calculating bouts that I added to the package is
intentionally different. In the upcoming version of GGIR (1.2-8) I
will have clarified this in the documentation, here is a preview of
that:

In the 2014 algorithm a 10 minute windows in which more than 80
percent of the epochs are above mvpathreshold (variable name
MVPA_E5S_B10M80._T100_ENMO) is considered an MVPA bout. Next, it
counts the entire window towards MVPA, so all 10 minutes. The new bout
definition (mvpa.2014 = FALSE) looks for a group or groups of epochs
with a value above mvpathreshold that span a time window of at least
10 minutes in which more than 80 percent of the epochs are above the
threshold. The motivation for the old definition was: A person who
spends 10 minutes in MVPA with a 2 minute break in the middle is
equally active as a person who spends 8 minutes in MVPA without taking
a break. Therefore, both should be counted equal and counted both as
10 minute MVPA bout. The motivation for the new definition is: not
counting breaks towards MVPA simplifies interpretation and still
counts the two persons in the example as each others equal.

In conclusion, you can use either of the two MVPA bout definition.
Both come with a different motivation and are not compatible. It is
important to clarify in your reports which one you used. Which one of
the two is better is not up to me to decide, but a matter of
definition and interpretation.

Vincent




On 9 May 2016 at 09:49, Vincent van Hees <vincent...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I have uploaded version 1.2-5 to CRAN.
>
> In recent weeks I discovered that the moderate and vigorous physical
> activity (MVPA) bout calculation in GGIR comes with a bug that causes
> the estimates of time spent in MVPA to be
> systematically larger then intended. The underlying code has been used
> by a number of publications since 2014, by which I cannot simply
> remove it.
>
> In the new version of the package I am using the corrected calculation
> as a default, but with the option to use the old calculation: To use
> the old calculation set argument mvpa.2014 = TRUE.
>
> If you choose to use the new calculation (default) then you will have
> the option to either count time
> spent in bouts including breaks (argument closedbouts=FALSE) or
> excluding the breaks (argument closedbouts=FALSE). So, either you
> count a 10 minute mvpa bout with a 1 minute break in the middle as 10
> minutes of mvpa or as 9 minutes of mvpa, respectively. I have no idea
> what the PA community normally does, but I think there could be a
> justification for both approaches, which is why I implemented both.
>
> I am fully aware that this kind of changes are not good for
> consistency of the science, but I think it is ultimately better to aim
> for the best possible calculation and discourage incorrect old
> calculations.
>
> The windows binaries of the new GGIR version 1.2-5 should be online in
> the upcoming 24 hours.
> At the moment when you apply bout calculation the code will print a
> warning message that the MVPA definition has been changed. I intend on
> modifying this message in the upcoming weeks as it is poorly written
> and printed too often. Therefore, I there will be a version 1.2-6 in
> the upcoming weeks with this turned off. However, I am not planning to
> make any more changes to the underlying calculations for the bout
> calculation.
>
> Best wishes,
>
> Vincent
